candidate.title: Cut Transition
candidate.problemStatement: Two exact product-world identities do not by themselves establish whether movement is authorized, compatible, recoverable, or safe, and updater-local selection may silently become movement authority.
candidate.scope: Provisional product-domain candidate for independently inspectable movement between exact Product Release Cuts; universal transition vocabulary, independent adoption, numbering, and separation from Warrant-bound Decision and Admission are not claimed.

observationPerspective.bearer: human and agent participants implementing selection, installation, activation, and rollback
observationPerspective.proximity: inside version comparison, manifest validation, artifact selection, and installer execution
consequences: bears selection, compatibility, migration, and rollback defects

genesis.observation: Exact endpoint identities left movement unresolved: identical, verified-successor, ancestor, recovery, diverged, and unknown relations require different decisions that cannot be inferred from root text, timestamps, SemVer, or network recency.
genesis.candidateObject: Cut Transition may be an independently addressable evidence-bearing relation that binds exact endpoints, compatibility, migration, rollback, trust, and movement authority without absorbing either endpoint or action execution.
genesis.claimBoundary: The cut opens qualification and does not decide whether Cut Transition is a Primitive, a typed Warrant/Decision/Admission record, an upgrade manifest section, or no new Primitive.

transformedPerspective.bearer: an operator or installed product deciding whether to move, remain, recover, or roll back
transformedPerspective.proximity: inside service continuity and rollback consequences but outside updater-local selection rules
consequences: bears unauthorized movement, incompatible activation, conflict, failed recovery, and unrecoverable rollback

genesis.transformation: The observer moved from choosing an artifact to bearing the consequences of movement between exact product worlds.
genesis.newlyVisibleNeed: Movement may require its own inspectable identity and evidence even when both endpoint Cuts remain valid and unchanged.
genesis.methodNotes: The strongest alternative is a Warrant-bound Decision followed by independent Admission; the implementation name does not defeat that alternative.

contactSides: exact source and target product worlds
participants authorizing and bearing upgrade, recovery, and rollback consequences
boundaryPressure.implicitHandling: Movement is inferred from SemVer precedence, channel order, timestamps, updater rules, network recency, or the presence of a newer artifact.

pressureChanges.description: Artifact availability and updater selection do not by themselves authorize product movement.
Movement may require migration, recovery, rollback, trust, and compatibility decisions.

observedFailures: Unequal roots are incorrectly ordered by version, timestamp, directory order, or recency.
An equal-SemVer conflict is mistaken for an update.
Rollback depends on a mutable source cache instead of exact retained evidence.
Valid endpoint identities are mistaken for authorization to move between them.
boundaryPressure.mediationClaim: A Cut Transition may keep exact endpoints and movement authority separately inspectable across update, recovery, and rollback.
boundaryPressure.internalObjectAlternative: Warrant-bound Decision plus independent Admission and a typed upgrade manifest may provide equivalent movement semantics.

pressure: Endpoint identity does not imply a safe or authorized relation.
Equal-SemVer worlds may be identical, successors, or conflicts.
Rollback and recovery require exact prior and target roots.
Updater execution must not create its own authority.
grounding.evidenceBoundary: The cut records one founding-adopter transition contract and public architecture at one exact Git cut. It contains no independent adopter, completed comparison with Warrant/Decision/Admission, cross-product transfer, or proof that a typed manifest relation is insufficient.
knownGaps: No decision between Primitive, typed authority record, manifest relation, and no-new-Primitive outcomes

alternatives.name: Warrant-bound Decision plus Admission
alternatives.reason: Existing KFD authority and settlement responsibilities may already express movement without a new Primitive.

alternatives.name: Typed upgrade manifest relation
alternatives.reason: A bounded relation inside an existing manifest may preserve exact endpoints, compatibility, migration, and rollback.

alternatives.name: SemVer and channel precedence
alternatives.reason: Products with immutable version mapping and simple trust may not need a separate transition object.

alternatives.name: No new Primitive
alternatives.reason: Cut Transition may remain Kungfu Profile vocabulary if deletion changes no decision beyond existing authority records.

contractModel.identity: One content-addressed root over exact source and target Cuts plus declared relation, compatibility, migration, rollback, trust, and evidence.
contractModel.boundary: Movement semantics between immutable endpoint Cuts; endpoint identity and installer occurrence remain separately owned.
contractModel.authority: May bind already granted movement authority; may not mint Warrant, make a Decision, admit an action, execute installation, or certify endpoints.
contractModel.lifecycle: Proposed, assessed, authorized or denied, executed or failed, observed, superseded, revoked, recovered, or rolled back without root mutation.

minimumClosure.notes: The contract closes one updater implementation, but existing authority and manifest alternatives have not been compared under fixed endpoints.

deletion.notes: Movement ambiguity is explicit; the incremental value beyond Warrant, Decision, Admission, and manifest relations remains unmeasured.

fuse.notes: Fusion with existing authority objects and manifest relations remains unresolved.

falsifiers: Warrant-bound Decision plus independent Admission preserves every movement consequence at lower ontology cost.
A typed manifest relation provides identical verification, recovery, and rollback behavior.
Products with immutable version mapping never need a separately addressable transition.
Independent adopters do not reproduce the movement-authority problem.

dogfood.notes: A public implementation witness exists, but fixed-endpoint comparison and independent KFD-5 review have not run.

decision.reason: Movement is operationally distinct from endpoint identity in one implementation, but minimum closure against Warrant-bound Decision, Admission, manifest relation, SemVer, and no-new-Primitive alternatives remains unproved.
residualRisks: The candidate may duplicate existing KFD authority and settlement objects.
Updater implementation details may be mistaken for universal transition semantics.
A transition record may launder unavailable or invalid endpoint evidence.
One implementation may overfit relation and rollback fields.
